one_liner: SIMD 'compacting' tokenizer for Zig source that beats the stdlib's hand-written tokenizer 2.75x on AVX-512 x86-64.
what_it_does: Re-implements Zig source tokenization using SIMD/SWAR bit-manipulation instead of the stdlib's per-character DFA (std.zig.Tokenizer), processing 64-byte chunks at a time. It ships as a single ~4,800-line main.zig benchmark harness whose only public entry point is `pub fn main()`; two experimental tokenizer variants sit alongside a call into the legacy std tokenizer used as the baseline. It is not a packaged library with a documented tokenize() API, and the AST/parser stage described in the repo name is still unimplemented.
how_it_is_fast: Computes per-64-byte-chunk bitstrings marking character classes (identifier/quote/comment/whitespace boundaries) via SIMD/SWAR so the cursor jumps via count-trailing-zeros instead of a branchy per-character loop. The 'compacting' variant additionally uses AVX-512 masked-compress/permute intrinsics (llvm.x86.avx512.mask.compress.q, avx512vbmi permvar) to pack token boundaries out of a chunk in parallel. Keywords/operators are matched with a compile-time perfect hash plus an array-mapped-trie bitmap (Bagwell-style) instead of DFA transitions, and tokens are stored as 1-byte lengths (with a 0-sentinel escape to a 4-byte length) rather than 32-bit start indices, cutting memory versus the stdlib tokenizer.
when_to_use: Batch/offline tokenization of large Zig corpora on AVX-512 x86-64 hardware (recent AMD or a 'beefy' Intel server) where raw GB/s throughput matters more than portability
You want a source-droppable reference for chunk-wise SIMD bitstring lexing tricks (perfect hashing, multiply-based movemask, sentinel padding) to adapt into your own tokenizer
Token memory footprint matters: the byte-length token encoding gets ~2.47x less memory than std's tokenizer in the author's test
You can pin a specific Zig 0.14 / -Doptimize=ReleaseFast toolchain and don't need long-term API stability
when_not_to_use: Any non-AVX-512 target (older x86-64, Apple Silicon/ARM, RISC-V, POWER/SPARC): the 2.75x number is AVX-512-only, and the README says the older 'Tokenizer 1' ARM/RISC-V code path 'has gone poof'
You need a stable, embeddable tokenizer API: this is a benchmark harness with `pub fn main()` as the only public function, not a packaged module
You need a full parser: AST generation is explicitly disabled/unimplemented in the harness (RUN_NEW_AST/RUN_LEGACY_AST off), and issue #2 ('parser design') is still open
You need conformant Unicode handling without checking current code state: the README repeatedly notes the UTF-8 validator being turned off during development
You want an actively maintained project: last commit 2025-04-16, and the author calls the project 'not ready for prime-time just yet'

integration.dependencies: jdz_allocator (pinned in build.zig.zon); vendored simdjson/simdjzon-derived UTF-8 validation code (Apache-2.0) inside main.zig
integration.min_toolchain: Zig 0.14 (build.zig.zon leaves minimum_zig_version unset; the verified benchmark used Zig 0.14 with -Doptimize=ReleaseFast)
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX-512 (avx512f/avx512bw/avx512vbmi) needed for the compacting tokenizer's benchmarked speed; SWAR and ARM NEON code paths exist in main.zig for other architectures but are not covered by the verified numbers
integration.thread_safety: not documented; no thread usage found in the source, harness runs single-threaded
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: does the same job as std.zig.Tokenizer conceptually, but the tokenizer logic lives as internal functions inside a benchmark main.zig rather than an exported library call, so using it means extracting the code yourself

gotchas: Compacting-tokenizer speed depends on specific AVX-512 intrinsics (mask.compress.q, avx512vbmi permvar/pshufb); hardware lacking these features uses different, unbenchmarked-here paths
The harness's printed line count (3,504,899,722 lines for ~47MB of source) is implausible and looks like a counting bug — trust the GB/s figures, not the derived loc/s numbers
Author notes legacy-tokenizer timings can shift ~15% from trivial code changes, so single-run comparisons are noisy
UTF-8 validation has been repeatedly disabled/re-enabled during development ('Currently the utf8 validator is turned off') — verify its state before relying on Unicode correctness
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over the flex/logos-family entries (LRSTAR, simd-lexing, Ragel, lexer-exp, logos) only if your workload is specifically Zig source on AVX-512 x86-64 and you want implementation ideas for a hand-rolled chunk-wise SIMD lexer; unlike Gigatoken or CrossDB it isn't a finished, general-purpose library, and it has no parser yet, so it's a reference/benchmark, not a drop-in replacement.
verified_claims_summary: On one run on a Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (Zig 0.14, -Doptimize=ReleaseFast) over a 3,253-file/~47MB user-assembled Zig source corpus, the AVX-512 'compacting' tokenizer reached 1.41 GB/s versus 0.51 GB/s for the mainline std.zig.Tokenizer used by the Zig 0.14 self-hosted compiler — a 2.75x throughput gain and ~2.47x less memory — measured as a single timed pass on the author's own laptop, not an independent benchmark suite.
status_note: Stale (last commit 2025-04-16) and explicitly not production-ready by the author's own account (parser unimplemented, UTF-8 validation toggled during development); MIT/Apache-2.0-licensed and small enough (~4.8k-line main.zig) to read or vendor, but expect to extract and rewire the tokenizer code rather than import it as a library.
